claims.text: Privacy concerns negatively influence user attitudes toward generative AI.
Privacy concerns positively predict personal protective behaviors in generative AI use.
Privacy concerns positively predict system-level protective behaviors in generative AI use.
Hallucination risk is negatively associated with user attitudes toward generative AI.
Hallucination risk positively predicts user information verification behaviors.
Information verification significantly moderates the relationship between user attitude and generative AI continuance intention.
Hallucination risk and system-level privacy-protective behaviors function as validated constructs for evaluating GenAI protective behaviors.

evidence.description: Privacy concerns negatively influence user attitudes
Privacy concerns positively predict personal protective behaviors based on structural equation modeling of survey data from 789 users.
Privacy concerns positively predict system-level protective behaviors based on structural equation modeling.
Hallucination risk is similarly associated with negative attitudes.
Hallucination risk positively predicts information verification.
Notably, only information verification significantly moderates the link between attitude and continuance intention.
developing and validating new constructs—hallucination risk and system-level privacy-protective behaviors.

methodologies.name: Structural Equation Modeling based on Protection Motivation Theory
methodologies.description: Analyzed survey data using structural equation modeling grounded in Protection Motivation Theory to examine direct and moderating risk-adaptive behaviors in GenAI adoption.
